tips.collect: Use tongs. Glochids are the real hazard, not the spines.
tips.handling: Macerate, rinse, dry thoroughly.

tips.cue: Schizocarp segments brown and separating from the central axis.
tips.collect: Roll the disc gently between fingers - ripe segments break away.
tips.handling: Hard seed coat; scarify before sowing.

tips.cue: Pappus (the fluff) has dried and begun to lift; heads look grey and open rather than green and tight.
tips.collect: Tug lightly - ripe achenes release with almost no resistance. If you have to pull, come back in a week.
tips.handling: Dries fast. Rub heads over a screen to separate achenes from chaff; many species have a high proportion of empty seed, so check fill by pinching.

tips.cue: Drupes fully dark red to purple-black and soft.
tips.collect: Hand-pick. Competition from wildlife is heavy.
tips.handling: Clean off flesh, then cold-moist stratify. Large seed, easy to handle and high viability.

tips.cue: Berries fully coloured and slightly soft.
tips.collect: Hand-pick whole berries.
tips.handling: Macerate and float off pulp. Most require both scarification and stratification, and are slow and unreliable from seed.

tips.cue: Varies with fruit type - fleshy fruits fully coloured and slightly soft, dry achenes brown and loose.
tips.collect: Pick fleshy fruit by hand; strip plumed achenes when they detach at a touch.
tips.handling: Clean pulp from fleshy fruit promptly - fermenting flesh kills seed. Most need cold-moist stratification.

tips.cue: Pods leathery to papery and turning brown; seeds rattle loose inside.
tips.collect: Many pods dehisce explosively - bag whole infructescences before they twist open, or check plants every few days.
tips.handling: Hard-coated seed benefits from scarification before sowing. Freeze or heat-treat to kill bruchid beetle larvae, which are common.

tips.cue: Drupes whitish and firm on a fresh cluster.
tips.collect: Take only from current-season clusters - the plant holds grey, empty fruit from previous years all the way through winter and spring.
tips.handling: Rub off the waxy coat, then scarify.
tips.caution: This is the species that most badly misleads a calendar-based model. Persistent old fruit generates fruiting records year-round; judge by cluster condition, not by date.

tips.handling: Winnow chaff gently; nutlets are small and blow away easily.
